Clinical outcomes for patients with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] in [[Danmark|Denmark]] are rigorously tracked to evaluate the effectiveness of cardiovascular care and stroke prevention strategies. The primary adverse events monitored are [[Iskæmisk apopleksi|ischemic stroke]] and [[Intrakraniel blødning|intracranial bleeding]], which serve as critical indicators of both disease progression and treatment safety. According to national data from [[Atrieflimren i Danmark]], the proportion of newly diagnosed patients who developed an ischemic stroke within one year was 1.1% between July 2021 and June 2022 [^src1], and slightly increased to 1.3% (Indicator 14) in the following year [^src4]. Similarly, the rate of intracranial bleeding within one year of diagnosis was 0.7% in 2021–2022 [^src1] and 0.8% (Indicator 13) in 2022–2023 [^src4]. Among prevalent patients, the development goal ([[Udviklingsmål]]) of keeping intracranial bleeding at or below 0.6% was successfully met [^src7]. Regional variations exist, with ischemic stroke rates among newly diagnosed patients ranging from 0.7% in [[Region Midtjylland]] to 1.4% in [[Region Sjælland]] [^src8].

A major determinant of these clinical outcomes is the administration and adherence to [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation treatment]]. In the 2018–2019 period, the national treatment rate was 87.3%, though it varied significantly across regions and clusters, ranging from 94.3% in [[Klynge SYD]] to 80.0% in [[Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] [^src2]. Long-term adherence remains a challenge; while 89.1% of patients were on anticoagulation one year post-diagnosis, this figure dropped to 87.3% after five years ([[Indikator 4a3]]) [^src3]. The choice of medication also influences outcomes: among prevalent patients, those treated with [[DOAC]] experienced a 0.86% ischemic stroke rate, compared to 0.88% for those on [[marevan]] [^src8]. Intracranial bleeding rates were comparable across treatment groups, though patients not receiving DOAC or Marevan had a slightly lower bleeding rate of 0.52% [^src8].

Beyond pharmacological interventions, non-clinical factors such as [[Patientuddannelse|patient education]] play a vital role in improving survival and reducing hospital readmissions. A comprehensive meta-analysis by [[Palm et al., 2020]] demonstrated that educational interventions led to a 22% reduction in the combined risk of death and readmission (Risk Ratio 0.78) compared to standard care without structured education [^src5], [^src9]. This highlights that optimizing clinical outcomes in atrial fibrillation requires a dual approach: precise medical management with anticoagulants and robust patient empowerment through education.
